title: Early Detection of Pulmonary Embolism in a General Patient Population Immediately Upon Hospital Admission Using Machine Learning to Identify New, Unidentified Risk Factors: Model Development Study.
summary: A random-forest model used pre-admission records from 2,568 patients with PE and 52,598 controls to predict PE at hospital admission. It achieved an 80% geometric mean of PE and non-PE classification accuracies; clustering identified subgroups with PE prevalence above 61%, including patients with prior PE or pneumonia. These are retrospective associations, not evidence of prospective clinical impact.
ai_technology: A random-forest model and two imbalance-handling methods used pre-admission demographics, comorbidities and medications to identify PE at hospital admission; clustering characterized high-risk subgroups.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: The primary abstract reports 2,568 PE cases and 52,598 controls, a random-forest model using pre-admission information, 80% geometric-mean classification accuracy, and risk-enriched clusters; hospital-admission PE prevalence was 4%.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective medical-record analysis does not establish prospective early diagnosis, external clinical generalization or improved patient outcomes; clustering identifies associations rather than causal PE risk factors.
